correctness.rationale: For n>=3, each graph has 2n horizontal edges and n rungs; arclength category probabilities yield 4/9,4/9,1/9. The proof obtains all HH/HV/VV means by elementary integrals. A Möbius rim path needs at most one rung (paired rung crossings can be removed by antipodal translation); only antipodally corresponding points within the same elementary edge require a 1/3 corrected expectation with probability 1/(2n). The central rung-pair tie contributes exactly 1/(6n) only at even n. Aggregation gives the displayed exact means and strict positive gaps for every integer n>=3. A separately implemented BFS/all-edge-pair rational clipping/integration program verifies both graphs at n=3,...,18, 192 exact assertions. The analytic argument, not finite tests, establishes the unrestricted theorem.

value.rationale: The prism and Möbius ladder have the same 2n vertices, 3n unit edges and total arclength, isolating the global topological twist. The resulting exact continuous first-moment gap is strictly positive with parity-dependent rational coefficient, whereas all odd-rung vertex means agree exactly. This supplies a natural complete comparison and explains when discrete network compactness misses a metric-graph distinction. Not a lone small-instance value or a disguised generic graph-computation restatement; scope is equal-edge first moments only.
